- Kind: repair — init.go's stat-then-write moved inside engine.WithFileLock (d719c53) with no new flag and no output change; the pre-existing success-path guards (TestInit_SparseWorkflowBlock's four cases, TestInit_CreatesTPGitignore) still pass untouched, and the freshly built binary still prints exactly {"created":"spec.tasks.json"} on success and exit 3 on the already-exists path.

Replacing engine.WithFileLock with a pass-through no-lock wrapper killed it and left the ENTIRE rest of the suite green — it is the only test covering this — restored byte-exact.

tasks.closed_reason:
- Kind: removal — §6.2's three forms were swept over the whole tree by an AST call-site census, and each of the 9 removals names what absorbed it: projectWorkflowOverride (a one-line pass-through) absorbed by its exported wrapper ProjectWorkflowOverride; DefaultWorkflow (1 caller) absorbed by ResolveWorkflowLayers; model.EffectiveLockTimeoutSeconds (1 caller) absorbed by engine.effectiveLockTimeoutSeconds; runAddBulk (1 caller) absorbed by runAdd; and 5 always-same-value parameters inlined as their constant — ProjectWorkflowOverride/LocalFlagDefaults/UpdateKeepList's start (10, 2 and 2 call sites, every one "."), rankFilesBySpecTerms' maxCount (2 sites, both 15) and readFilesContent's maxPerFile (2 sites, both 5000).
- Helpers with one call site, interfaces with one implementation, and always-constant parameters were enumerated mechanically, not by eye: an AST census over every .go file in the repo counted call sites per declaration and compared printed argument text per parameter position. Interfaces are vacuous here — the tree declares zero interface types (verified by search over internal/ and cmd/). The census's first constant-parameter pass returned zero because a call's own Fun identifier was double-recorded as an argument-less reference; it was fixed and re-proved to discriminate (loosening the threshold still returned nothing, which is what exposed the bug) before any of its findings were acted on.
- Indirection kept is named with its second caller: EffectiveGateTimeoutSeconds has four (gate.go:50, gate.go:56, gate.go:73, review_status.go:187); ScopeFenceText has three (brief.go:506, brief_assemble_test.go:35, brief_test.go:10); LoadKeepList, DiscoverTPDir, ProjectRoot and the rest of the start-parameter family keep it because a caller passes a different value (resume.go:48 passes start to LoadKeepList; DiscoverTPDir has 17 varied callers); readFilesContent's maxTotal stays because the doc and test prompts pass 30000 and 20000. Two are kept over a reason rather than a caller, stated plainly: EffectiveReviewMaxRounds and EffectiveAuditMaxRounds each have one caller, but both sit in one struct literal in resume.go, so inlining them writes the identical 0-50 clamp twice into one function — §6.1 duplication traded for §6.2 indirection, and Non-Goal 7 forbids a shared helper.
